  "situation": "The ship had received a rules‑of‑engagement brief that warned of a significant danger from indiscriminate attacks and required ships to identify unknown aircraft. The brief also gave the commander authority and responsibility to take all possible protective measures and to use necessary and proportional force in self‑defence. On 21 February the commanding officer was briefed that an Iraqi aircraft was operating over the northern Persian Gulf and instructed the tactical action officer to monitor track 2202. Radar later detected an unknown aircraft on a converging course with a four‑nautical‑mile closest‑point‑of‑approach, and the tactical action officer warned the commanding officer and sought permission to issue a warning on the Military Air Distress frequency. The commanding officer, through the lieutenant, denied permission to transmit the warning. At the time, the CIWS and fire‑control positions were vacant. The aircraft subsequently launched two Exocet missiles that struck the ship.",
